span.p: format ^[A-Z]{2,4}[0-9]{3}$ — unique across Courses (409 on duplicate).\nPersisted by CourseCodeConverter to courses.course_code VARCHAR.

div.style: text-align: center; white-space: break-spaces; display: table; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; width: 200px;

span.p: 10 or 13 digits — unique across Books (409 on duplicate).\nPersisted by IsbnConverter to books.isbn VARCHAR.

div.style: text-align: center; white-space: break-spaces; display: table; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; width: 200px;

span.p:
Published API of the student module: book and enrollment both store it.
As an ENTITY ID it is NOT the mapped field — Student keeps @Id @GeneratedValue
Long id and exposes id() : StudentId. @EmbeddedId with @GeneratedValue does not
work in Hibernate; do not attempt it.
As Book.ownerId it IS mapped, by StudentIdConverter : AttributeConverter~StudentId, Long~
to books.student_id BIGINT NULL.

div.style: text-align: center; white-space: break-spaces; display: table; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; width: 200px;

span.p: credits must be positive (@Positive on the request DTO,\nCHECK (credits > 0) in the schema, guarded again in changeCredits).

div.style: text-align: center; white-space: break-spaces; display: table; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; width: 200px;

span.p:
existsBy*(x) answers create-time uniqueness.
existsBy*AndIdNot(x, id) answers UPDATE-time uniqueness — the
same check EXCLUDING the row being updated. Using the first form
on a PUT makes a student conflict with their own studentCode.
See ../sequences/update-student.mmd.

div.style: text-align: center; white-space: break-spaces; display: table; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; width: 200px;

span.p:
identity IS (studentId, courseId), mapped as @EmbeddedId EnrollmentId
holding RAW Longs — nesting converted value objects inside an @EmbeddedId is
where this design stops being worth it. studentId() and courseId() wrap on read.
Uniqueness of the pair is the no-duplicate-enrolment invariant, enforced by
EnrollmentService and by the composite PRIMARY KEY on student_courses.

div.style: text-align: center; white-space: break-spaces; display: table; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; width: 200px;

span.p:
single-owner invariant, and it lives HERE rather than in a service because it
reads only the book's own state:
 assignTo(y) on a book owned by x != y throws InvalidRelationshipException (409)
 assignTo(x) on a book already owned by x is idempotent
 release() is idempotent

div.style: text-align: center; white-space: break-spaces; display: table; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; width: 200px;

span.p: the duplicate-enrollment rule lives in the SERVICE, not on the entity,\nbecause it needs a repository lookup. An entity that holds a repository\nis not an entity. That asymmetry with Book is deliberate.

div.style: text-align: center; white-space: break-spaces; display: table; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; width: 200px;

span.p:
deleting a Student does NOT cascade to Books. StudentService publishes
StudentDeleted BEFORE removing the row; the book module releases owned books
and the enrollment module drops enrollments, synchronously, in the same
transaction. See ../sequences/delete-student.mmd.
